metrics.reason: source insufficient: theta/beta/lambda, iteration tolerance, damping, discretisation, float properties and tension unit not given

discrepancies.target: Table 2 item 16 buoyed vs unbuoyed element weight
discrepancies.observation: Adding buoyant material raises the element weight in air by 350 dN (3836 -> 4186) and the weight in water by 338 dN (3243 -> 3581). The implied added buoyancy is 12 dN, i.e. a displaced volume of 0.012 m³ and an implied density of about 29 000 kg/m³ for the added material.
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: A buoyant material of 60.96 cm OD around the 40.64 cm riser displaces about 2.22 m³ per 15.24 m element (Figure 3 geometry, choke/kill lines excluded), so the in-water weight should fall by roughly 1840 dN, not rise. The tabulated buoyed w_p (or its definition) is inconsistent with the stated buoyancy. EngiProof does not choose a corrected value.
closure_requirements: Preserve the printed w_a and w_p values.
Resolve only with an erratum, the API 2J source data or equivalent primary evidence.
Do not substitute an inferred buoyed weight.

discrepancies.target: Table 1 head tensions for 457.20 m and 914.40 m (cases 3-6)
discrepancies.observation: Printed 1.290.500 dN and 2.225.000 dN imply 662 MPa and 1141 MPa axial stress in the 40.64/37.46 cm riser pipe and 6-23 times the tabulated submerged weight; cases 1-2 (53.400, 89.000 dN) imply 27 and 46 MPa and 1.6-2.6 times.
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: All other Table 1/2 values are SI renderings of round imperial quantities; cases 1-2 equal 120 and 200 kips, while cases 3-6 equal 2901 and 5002 kips - ten times 290 and 500 kips. A one-place grouping/decimal error is plausible but is not established by the source. The printed values are preserved and not corrected.
closure_requirements: Resolve only with API Bulletin 2J (1977) case data, an erratum, or equivalent primary evidence.

discrepancies.target: 1200 m example head tension T = 298 (1 + 0,2 sin 2 pi t/9)
discrepancies.observation: No unit is given for 298. The mud-filled riser of Table 3 has an effective weight of 3.46 MN (2.45 MN with ideal massless floats over the full length).
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: Only a unit of order 10 kN (e.g. tonne-force, giving a mean of 2.92 MN) supports the riser weight; N, dN and kN do not. Even then the minimum tension (0.8 x 298) is below the ideal-float effective weight. The unit is not asserted, and float coverage/mass are not given.
closure_requirements: Do not assign a unit without primary evidence.
Record float coverage and mass if a source provides them.

discrepancies.observation: The printed equation reads Y = 7.70 sin(2 pi t/g); the preceding sentence states a sinusoidal variation with a period of 9 s and an amplitude of 7.70 m, and the tension equation on the same page uses 2 pi t/9.
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: Most likely a typographical 'g' for '9'. The tool uses the period stated in the source text; the printed equation is preserved.
closure_requirements: Preserve both the printed equation and the text statement.

discrepancies.target: Meaning of 'amplitude' of the prescribed head displacement (Table 2 item 20, 1.22 m)
discrepancies.observation: Figures 4(a)-9(a) show head-end envelopes centred on the Table 2 static offsets (within 0.2 m) with total widths of 1.25-1.54 m (measurement uncertainty 0.05-0.33 m), consistent with 1.22 m peak-to-peak and not with +/-1.22 m (2.44 m width).
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: The author uses 'amplitude' for trough-to-crest height elsewhere ('amplitude (through-to-crest) of 6 m'; p. 220 calls the Table 2 wave height of 6.096 m an 'amplitude'), but uses single amplitude in Y = 7.70 sin(...). The figures support peak-to-peak for the six comparison cases. EngiProof records this without redefining Table 2.
closure_requirements: Resolve with API 2J case definitions or equivalent primary evidence.

discrepancies.target: Figure 11 '~15%' linear-structure stress underestimate near the riser head
discrepancies.observation: From the Figure 11 labels (linear: +27.20/-22.45, nonlinear: +26.24/-31.40 dN/mm²), the peak absolute stress is 13.4% lower in the linear analysis (nonlinear exceeds linear by 15.4%). Per envelope, the linear analysis is 28.5% lower on the minimum envelope and 3.7% higher on the maximum envelope.
discrepancies.engineering_interpretation: The '~15%' statement is reproduced only when read as the peak absolute bending stress near the head; it does not hold per envelope. The maximum-envelope label attribution is less certain (overlapping spikes); the alternative attribution gives 16.4%/19.7%. The underlying stresses are not recomputed.
closure_requirements: Preserve the printed labels and the claim.
Resolve only with the original analysis output or an author statement of the metric.

limitations: The nonlinear dynamic riser responses of Figures 4-9 and 11 are not reproduced (P45-C009 BLOCKED): theta, beta, lambda of Eq. (7), the iteration tolerance and limit of Appendix 3, the structural damping, the element discretisation of cases 1-6, and the float coverage/mass of the 1200 m example are not given; the 1200 m tension unit is missing (P45-D003).
No SOLVER_NEW evidence is produced. The only integrator is an INDEPENDENT single-degree-of-freedom reconstruction whose t+tau -> t+dt step is not in the source.
Only the head-end tips of Figures 4(a)-9(a) are digitized; Figures 4(b)-9(b) and 10 are source-reviewed only. Figure 11 is used through its printed labels.
Figure 11 maximum-envelope label attribution is a visual reading with MEDIUM confidence.

The comparison programs of Figures 4-9 are identified only as 'eight other programs' (API Bulletin 2J, 1977); agreement between RISER and those envelopes is published evidence, not independent validation.
Source PDF and page images are external to the repository; the SHA-256 and page locators are retained.

verification_tolerance.statement: Recomputation-equivalence tolerance only. The study-wide default (rel 1e-9, abs 1e-12) is unchanged. One path-scoped entry covers the independent beam-column FE check. It is NOT an engineering acceptance or validation tolerance and does not relax any comparison with the published source.

path_tolerances.rationale: The independent FE solve of Appendix 1 (numpy.linalg on a fine mesh) differs across NumPy/BLAS builds and operating systems. Measured in CI on 27 September 2026 (Linux Python 3.10-3.13 with NumPy 2.2.6-2.5.3, Windows Python 3.10/3.13, macOS arm64 Python 3.13): FE stiffness and reaction values change by <= 2.9e-7 absolute (<= 5e-8 relative), and the FE-vs-Appendix-1 residual max_relative_difference (1.6e-8 to 3.2e-8) changes by <= 1e-8 absolute. The engineering statement is the boolean appendix1_matches_independent_fe (every residual < 1e-6), which is compared exactly and stays material if it flips.
